# Environment that actually produced every number in docs/ and results/.
#
# This is not requirements.txt. Those pins (numpy==2.2.6, torch==2.6.0) are the versions the project
# was written against originally; A-31 in docs/11_code_audit.md measures what happens when you install
# them and re-run: the arena's geometry and randomisation streams are bit-identical, but the first PPO
# update differs at 1e-6 and every saved checkpoint differs after 4,000 steps. So requirements.txt
# describes an arena, and this file describes the measurements.
#
# Generated by `python -m pip freeze` inside an isolated virtualenv (no --system-site-packages) on
# Python 3.10.11 / Windows. Verified equivalent to the environment that ran the study:
#   scripts/train_rl.py --seed 42 --steps 4000
# produces byte-identical checkpoints and training_log.json in both, matching the hashes recorded in
# docs/09_reproducibility.md section 9.6.
#
# torch is the CUDA build (2.5.1+cu121) from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121; every reported
# measurement ran on CPU, because docs/11_code_audit.md#gpu-and-thread-scaling shows CUDA is slower
# for this workload.
#
# Not included: mlflow (every experiment-2 run in the study used --no-mlflow, so no committed number
# depends on it) and ursina/panda3d (rendering only; see the trailer block at the bottom).

colorama==0.4.6

iniconfig==2.3.1

# --- rendering only, not used by any measurement ---------------------------------------------
# docs/assets/gameplay_exp*.gif were produced in a second isolated env on the same interpreter:
#   ursina==6.1.2, Panda3D==1.10.16, panda3d-gltf==1.3.0, panda3d-simplepbr==0.13.1
#   numpy==1.26.4, pillow==12.3.0, ImageIO==2.37.4, imageio-ffmpeg==0.6.0
# Ursina is deliberately absent from the block above: installing it changes nothing about the
# numbers, and keeping it out means the measurement environment stays small enough to rebuild.
